fieldMarks: Grizzled gray coat; bushy tail with 5–10 alternating black and brown rings
Stocky with short legs, pointed snout and short rounded ears
behavior: Mainly nocturnal; family groups forage together at night and den by day
Omnivorous: crayfish, corn, fruit, nuts, eggs, insects; raids garbage in towns
In the north dens through winter on stored fat (not true hibernation)
Handles food with the front paws, the source of the 'washing' reputation
habitat: Anywhere with water, food and den sites; best in hardwood swamps, floodplain forest, marshes and farmland; very common in cities.
range: Southern Canada (all provinces except Newfoundland and Labrador), the United States except parts of the Rockies and desert Southwest, and south to Panama; expanding northward.
